functional_compartments.name: Iliocostal fiber bundle
functional_compartments.function_note: Iliac crest to 12th rib -- the most consistently described fiber direction, per Bogduk et al.'s three-bundle model of quadratus lumborum.
functional_compartments.source: Phillips S, Mercer S, Bogduk N (2008) Proc Inst Mech Eng H 222(2):151-159 -- anatomy and biomechanics of quadratus lumborum, describing its three fiber bundle layers (anterior/iliocostal, middle/lumbocostal, posterior/iliolumbar) (corrects an earlier draft's citation of Bogduk, Macintosh & Pearcy 1992, which models lumbar erector spinae and multifidus but does not cover quadratus lumborum -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md)

functional_compartments.name: Iliolumbar fiber bundle
functional_compartments.function_note: Iliac crest to lumbar transverse processes L1-L4 -- the second of the muscle's three documented fiber bundles.
functional_compartments.source: Phillips S, Mercer S, Bogduk N (2008) Proc Inst Mech Eng H 222(2):151-159 -- anatomy and biomechanics of quadratus lumborum, describing its three fiber bundle layers (anterior/iliocostal, middle/lumbocostal, posterior/iliolumbar) (corrects an earlier draft's citation of Bogduk, Macintosh & Pearcy 1992, which models lumbar erector spinae and multifidus but does not cover quadratus lumborum -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse scan in the posterior axillary line, between the 12th rib and the iliac crest, angled to capture the 'shamrock sign' -- quadratus lumborum, psoas major and erector spinae arranged around the L2-L3 transverse process like three leaflets. Three named approaches target different tissue planes: lateral (QL1, needle at the muscle's anterolateral border, injectate between QL and transversus abdominis), posterior (QL2, needle posterior to QL, injectate between QL and erector spinae/latissimus dorsi aponeurosis), and anterior/transmuscular (QL3, needle passed through QL to its anterior surface, injectate between QL and psoas major).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Retroperitoneal, posterior abdominal wall; deep to the transversus abdominis aponeurosis and thoracolumbar fascia. The QL3/transmuscular approach places the needle tip anterior to the muscle, adjacent to psoas major and close to the lower pole of the kidney.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The 'shamrock sign' -- QL, psoas major and erector spinae forming three leaflets around the transverse process on transverse ultrasound -- is the standard landmark used to orient all three approaches.
structures_at_risk: kidney (lower pole lies close to the muscle's anterosuperior surface, particularly relevant to the QL3/transmuscular approach)
peritoneum and abdominal viscera, anterior to the muscle
lumbar plexus branches (subcostal, iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal, genitofemoral and femoral nerve roots) running within or adjacent to the muscle and psoas
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: One of the most extensively published ultrasound-guided truncal fascial plane blocks of the past decade, used for analgesia after abdominal, urological and hip surgery; nomenclature (QL1/QL2/QL3) established by El-Boghdadly et al. distinguishes the approaches by needle trajectory relative to the muscle rather than by a single technique. The anterior/transmuscular (QL3) approach has also been used therapeutically outside the perioperative setting, e.g. with added steroid for chronic myofascial flank pain.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: El-Boghdadly K, Elsharkawy H, Short A, Chin KJ (2016) Reg Anesth Pain Med 41(4):548-549, doi:10.1097/AAP.0000000000000411 -- QLB nomenclature and anatomical considerations (PubMed); Theeraratvarasin C et al. (2024) Medicine (Baltimore) 103(28):e38887, doi:10.1097/MD.0000000000038887 -- randomized trial of ultrasound-guided anterior (QL3) block technique in kidney transplantation (PubMed); Niraj G (2023) Pain Pract 23(6):689-694, doi:10.1111/papr.13223 -- transmuscular QLB with steroid for chronic myofascial flank pain (PubMed)
